segments.say: The places of tonight have faded now, and all that's left is a soft, warm quiet, like the inside of a blanket on a winter morning. You don't need to picture anything anymore. You don't need to follow any path. Just rest here, in the dark, and let your breathing be slow and easy. Everything is calm, and everything can wait until morning.

Notice your breath, without changing it. The air comes in, cool and soft. It pauses for a moment. And it goes out again, warm and slow. In, and out. In, and out. Each breath is a little slower than the one before it, a little deeper, a little softer, like waves on a quiet shore growing further and further apart.

Let's take ten slow breaths together, counting down. You don't have to reach the end. Ten, breathing in, and out. Nine, in, and slowly out. Eight, softer now. Seven, the body heavier. Six, the mind quieter. Five, halfway, and sinking. Four, warm and loose. Three, almost there. Two, so heavy. One. And rest.

The night is long enough for every memory to soften. Whatever came back to you this evening, the small slips, the words that came out wrong, the moments that made your face grow warm, they're already a little further away than they were. Sleep will carry them further still. And in the morning, they'll be smaller, and lighter, and perhaps a little bit funny.

show.text: The night is long enough for every memory to soften.

segments.say: Picture, just for a moment, a quiet window at night, with pale moonlight falling softly across a folded quilt. A closed book rests on a small table. A cup sits beside it, long since empty. Beyond the glass the sky is silver and blue, and a few faint stars are keeping watch. Nothing is moving. Everything is resting. And so can you.

Somewhere, Ivy is fast asleep now, her face soft against the cool side of the pillow. The memory that woke her at a quarter past one has gone quiet, like a guest who finally said goodnight and closed the door gently behind them. In the morning, if she remembers it at all, she might just smile, and shake her head, and get on with her day.

And for you, a small reminder, the last one tonight. Feeling embarrassed is not a sign that something is wrong with you. It's a sign that you care about other people, and about how you make them feel. That's a good thing to care about. It's one of the most human things there is. So let it rest now, and rest along with it.

Caring how you seem is a sign of caring about others. The warmth that rose in your cheeks tonight came from the same place as your kindness, your wish to fit in, to be good company, to do right by the people around you. That's not something to fix. It's something to be gentle with. So be gentle with it now, and with yourself.

show.text: Caring how you seem is a sign of caring about others.

segments.say: Feel how heavy your body has become. Your head rests deep in the pillow. Your shoulders have sunk into the mattress. Your arms lie loose at your sides, and your legs are long and still. The bed holds every part of you, so you don't have to hold anything at all. Breathe in, slow and soft. Breathe out, and sink a little further.

Before you sleep, just notice these few small things. Your body is heavy, and the bed is holding all of it. Your breath is slow, rising and falling on its own. Your mind is quiet, wide and soft like a field of snow. And you are safe, here, tonight, in the dark. Nothing more is needed.

If a thought drifts in, let it drift out again, like a leaf on the slow river. If a sound reaches you, let it pass, like a car on a distant road. If your mind wanders, let it wander softly, and fall asleep wherever it lands. Sleep doesn't need to be chased. It comes on its own, when everything else has been put down.

Goodnight. Goodnight to Ivy, sleeping under her quilt. Goodnight to the lanterns on the river, and the snow on the village roofs, and the embers glowing low in the cottage fire. Goodnight to you, with your heavy hands, your soft face, and your slow, warm breath. You've done enough for today. Let sleep come gently now.

Every new morning is a fresh page. Whatever you said or did today, or nine years ago, tomorrow doesn't hold it against you. It simply arrives, quietly, with a new light at the window. And until then, the night is here to look after you, slowly and kindly, all the way through until dawn.

show.text: Every new morning is a fresh page.

segments.say: Around you, the house is quiet too. The walls are resting, the floors are resting, the windows are resting. Somewhere a clock ticks softly, slower than you remember. Outside, the street is still, and the trees are still, and the sky is wide and patient. The whole world has lowered its voice for you, and it will keep it low until morning.

There's nothing more to do now. Nowhere to be, nothing to answer, nothing to prove. Your body is warm, and your mind is still. Rest here. Breathe slowly. Let the quiet hold you. Everything that needed to happen today has happened, and everything else can wait until the morning comes.

And if, one day soon, you meet someone whose face you know perfectly, but whose name has completely vanished from your mind, and you stand there smiling, searching, hoping they won't notice, there's a reason for that too. It's a gentle and fascinating one, and we'll find it together, when we meet again.
Why does a face stay with you for years, while the name slips away in seconds? Rest well tonight, and next time, we'll find out.
